name: Zaika Restaurant (JKTDC Tourist Establishment)
signature_dish: fried trout (sourced from adjacent government farm)
why_it_matters: JKTDC's Zaika sits inside the Kokernag botanical garden, with Asia's largest trout farm next door — guests can buy fresh trout from the Fisheries Department counter and the in-house cook fries it for them. Reviewers consistently praise the small-batch paneer and a less-oily rogan josh than the Delhi norm.
insider_tip: Walk to the trout-farm sales counter first (open mornings), pick a 400-500g fish, then hand it to Zaika's kitchen — they'll fry it in mustard oil for a small charge. Order paneer-tomato or dal as the side; the menu is otherwise short.
signature_address: JKTDC Tourist Establishment, Kokernag Botanical Garden, Anantnag District 192202

name: Wild Trout Cafe (The Heritage Resort)
why_it_matters: Private-sector counterpoint to the JKTDC kitchen — the in-house cafe at Heritage Resort Bidder Kokernag focuses its short menu on locally-sourced trout, plus standard Kashmiri and Indian comfort plates. One of the few year-round options in Kokernag once the day-tour buses leave.
insider_tip: Call ahead to confirm trout is on (+91 99068 28311) — supply tracks the farm's daily catch. Out-of-season visitors sometimes find only Kashmiri/Indian dishes.
signature_address: The Heritage Resort, Ward No. 6, Bidder, Kokernag, Anantnag District 192202

name: Cafe 13
why_it_matters: Peertakiya's modern cafe — pizza, burgers, wazwan platters — that fills the gap for travellers who don't want a third lunch of dal-rajma. Locals describe it as 'one of the better options in a town that has very few eating places'.
insider_tip: Service can drag even when the room is empty; if you have a bus to catch back to Srinagar order takeaway from the counter rather than dining in.
signature_address: Peertakiya, Near JK Bank, Kokernag, Anantnag District 192202
